boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Kennesaw Mountain record (June 27, 1864) in Atlanta Campaign [May-September 1864]. It falls inside the Marietta aggregate (GA013), which does not repeat its figures. Schofield's advance beyond Olley's Creek the same day is part of Cox's account but not the assaults. The live NPS page labels the campaign "Morgan's Raid Into Kentucky" and dates it May-September 1864; neither field replaces the frozen campaign or battle interval. Campaign-wide totals are context and are not assigned to this record. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force fields name the two armies without counts; the live field reads zero. Cox says only three points were selected for assault, the middle attacked by two columns each with a two-company front; he names Newton's and Davis's divisions and Morgan L. Smith's division with Walcutt's brigade, and says Loring's corps held the mountain. Johnston calls it a general advance.
claims.rationale: Formations, not counts; the scope of the attack is described differently. None is adopted. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Cox says Newton's columns were stopped at the entanglement of felled trees before the works, that Smith's division climbed a steep rocky slope choked with felled trees, and that Davis's men crossed rocky, rough and tangled ground. He cites French's report on how the mountain let the Confederates watch every Union movement. NPS says attacking an entrenched enemy was futile.
claims.rationale: Ground described by an interested history and a summary; no map verification. The Kennesaw line was occupied on June 19 and prepared by Confederate engineers, but no inherited tag is assigned without a timing review.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Confederate victory. Johnston says the advance was everywhere repulsed with heavy loss. Cox says the one chance to break through was tried and lost; Sherman called Schofield's position beyond Olley's Creek the only advantage of the day. NPS says the fighting ended by noon with high Union casualties.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live casualty texts read 4,000 (US 3,000; CS 1,000). Cox gives Sherman's loss as about twenty-five hundred, says about eight hundred fell at the head of each of the three assaults, and that Johnston admits over five hundred. Johnston reports Hardee's figures of 195 lost in Cheatham's division against 2,000 enemy and 11 in Cleburne's against 1,000, and Loring's 236 against Union estimates of 2,500 to 3,000.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Johnston's own-side components sum to 442 (a computation here, excluding other commands); the enemy figures are estimates, and Cox's 2,500 and the frozen 3,000 differ.

open_questions: Sherman's, Thomas's, Howard's, Palmer's, Newton's, Davis's and Logan's June 28 reports (the last seen at a range boundary), French's report, Hardee's Kenesaw loss addendum (read, not selected) and the compiled returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Cox's Atlanta (Scribner, 1882) is a second: a retrospective Union history by the Twenty-third Corps division commander, drawing on official reports and memoirs, so it is not independent of them. Johnston's October 20, 1864 report, printed in Volume XXXVIII Part 3, is a third family (interested Confederate account). Official Records Series I Volume XXXVIII is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Campaign-wide strength and loss totals are context, not assigned to one record.
